findings.title: Directory drag-and-drop performs one render-triggering update per file
findings.what: walkDirectory invokes the progress callback after every admitted file, and the callback immediately calls setScannedCount. Each asynchronous file lookup can therefore cause another render. The handler also accumulates every File handle in recursive arrays and allFiles before the worker pipeline begins, with no loose-directory entry budget. A large ~/.claude selection can spend substantial main-thread time scanning and rendering before parsing starts.
findings.fix: Throttle progress updates by time or batch, enforce an admitted-file limit during directory traversal, and feed bounded batches to the pipeline where feasible.
findings.acceptance: A deterministic directory-walk benchmark with at least 10,000 admitted files completes within a documented budget, performs a bounded number of progress state updates independent of file count, and rejects selections over the configured file limit with a clear status.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed that src/components/FileUpload.tsx:95-106 calls progress once per accepted file and src/components/FileUpload.tsx:227-233 binds that callback directly to setScannedCount while retaining all returned files. The worker handoff at lines 246 and 150-160 occurs only after traversal, so worker parsing does not mitigate this scan/render path.

findings.title: Out-of-order live polls can restore stale session state
findings.what: setInterval invokes poll without an in-flight or generation guard. If poll A remains pending while poll B starts and B resolves first, A can later call setLive with older data, reverting the widget to a stale session or resurrecting a session after a newer inactive response.
findings.fix: Serialize polls with recursive setTimeout after settlement, or attach a monotonically increasing request generation and apply only the newest response.
findings.acceptance: Add a test using two deferred fetchLive promises: resolve the second with {active:false}, then resolve the first with active data, and verify the component remains inactive; the test must pass with the implemented ordering guard.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass confirmed the only guard at src/components/LiveSession.tsx:124 is component cancellation, not request ordering. The existing polling test at src/components/LiveSession.test.ts:139-164 resolves requests in order and therefore does not cover the reproducible stale-response sequence.

findings.title: Live polling permits unbounded concurrent requests
findings.what: The 10-second interval starts poll regardless of whether the preceding fetchLive call has settled. During sustained endpoint latency or a hung request, concurrent requests grow once per interval for the lifetime of the mounted widget.
findings.fix: Allow only one in-flight poll and schedule the next poll after it settles; retain the unmount cancellation guard.
findings.acceptance: With fetchLive held pending while fake time advances across at least five intervals, assert it is called exactly once; after resolving it, assert exactly one subsequent poll is scheduled.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read verified that src/components/LiveSession.tsx:128-129 starts the initial poll and an unconditional interval, with no pending flag or abort controller. The test at src/components/LiveSession.test.ts:139-164 checks timer cleanup only and supplies immediately resolved requests.
